_howto: Copy this, fill it in, and propose it BEFORE doing any work:
The operator confirms it (queue.ps1 -ConfirmAnchor), and only then does work begin.
Write it in the OPERATOR's terms, not yours. If you had to guess at what they meant,
the anchor is where you say so - that is the cheapest moment to be corrected.
goal: One sentence. The outcome, in the operator's words, not a description of the steps.
artifact: path/to/the/file.md - and what KIND of thing it is (an operator README, a patch, a test, a report).
audience: Who reads or runs this, and what they already know. 'An operator who has never brought this plane up' produces a different document than 'a maintainer auditing the compose file'.
acceptance: Each entry must be checkable by someone who did not do the work.
Say what would count as FAILING it, not only what passing looks like.
This list is what the tester tests. If it is not here, it will not be verified.
out_of_scope: Name the tempting adjacent work this deliberately does not do.
Findings about problems elsewhere are real, and they still do not belong in the artifact.
findings_sink: documentation/notes/<topic>-findings.md - where anything true but out of scope gets written down instead of being pasted into the deliverable or discarded. HELD TO THE SAME STANDARD AS THE ARTIFACT: a claim here about what a script does is verified against that code path, not against its comments. An unverified sink is worse than no sink - it looks like a record, and the next item acts on it.
